title: From Open Banking to Open Branching: Facing Bank Branches Closures with a New Technological Standard in Europe
content: The growing phenomenon of bank branch closures, driven by increasing operational costs and the need to meet specific KPIs, represents a significant challenge for both customers and banks. The closure of branches, especially in remote areas, reduces access to banking services and damages the image and influence of banks in the community, undermining customer trust. To address this issue, a potential solution draws inspiration from the experience of Open Banking, which has revolutionized the financial sector through digitalization. The idea is to extend this philosophy to bank branches, creating what can be defined as "Open Branching" (OB). This term refers to a technology-enabled branch where all services traditionally offered in-person can also be accessed digitally. Open Branching allows branches to offer a wide range of digital services through APIs (Application Programming Interfaces), maintaining the interface and experience of a traditional branch while enhancing accessibility and efficiency by integrating the physical and digital worlds. In collaboration with a major Italian Bank and the Bank of Italy as part of the MilanoHub program, we developed and standardized a taxonomy of key branch-customer products and services, categorized by type (e.g., with and without authentication, account information, loans, withdrawals), and released it under an open-source license. This standard enable third-party operators to enhance the Customer Experience in traditional branches, much like Open Banking has done with online services. The validity of the standard was demonstrated through a case study focused on branch service access through the Metaverse, highlighting the effectiveness and potential of this innovation.
